 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Sports Sports Joshua Pacio submits Keito Yamakita to retain ONE strawweight title 
 By RAFAEL BANDAYREL Published November 18, 2026 11:38pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Photo: ONE Championship Joshua Pacio successfully defended his ONE Strawweight MMA World Championship, submitting Keito Yamakita in the fourth round of their main event clash at ONE SAMURAI 5 on Wednesday evening.
 The official stoppage came at the 4:17 mark of round four at EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo, Japan, as Pacio secured another impressive title victory on enemy territory.
 The Japanese challenger controlled much of the opening round, lifting Pacio and slamming him onto the canvas before taking him down again after they returned to their feet. Yamakita then caught the champion in a reverse triangle choke, forcing Pacio to focus on defending the submission attempt for the remainder of the round.
 The second round saw both fighters trade submission attempts on the ground. Yamakita initiated a takedown, but Pacio managed to threaten with a leg lock before the challenger escaped. The Filipino eventually worked his way into mount position and closed the round with a series of hammer fists.

 Pacio maintained control in the third round, keeping Yamakita on the canvas and working from the top position. Although the challenger managed to defend against the champion’s ground-and-pound, he struggled to mount any significant offense.
 The defending champion finally found the finish in the fourth round, locking in an arm-triangle choke that rendered Yamakita unconscious.
 The victory improved Pacio’s professional record to 25-5 and gave him his first career win in Japan. It also marked his second consecutive title win by submission, further cementing his reputation as one of the division’s most dangerous grapplers.
 —JKC, GMA News
